text: According to the Mill-Ramsey-Lewis Best System Analysis, a regularity counts as a law of nature if and only if it does what?
choices: Appears as an axiom or theorem in the true deductive system that best balances simplicity and strength.
Is underwritten by a necessitation relation between the universals it mentions.
Follows from the essential natures of the natural kinds it concerns.
Is a true universal generalization whose instances are contiguous in space and time.
explanation: The BSA distinguishes laws from accidental generalizations by theoretical role: laws belong to the systematization of all particular facts that optimally trades simplicity against strength (with 'fit' added for probabilistic laws). Options 1 and 2 are the anti-Humean rivals (DTA and dispositional essentialism) the BSA explicitly rejects, since Lewis refuses any law-making relation or modal primitive beyond the Humean mosaic.
